drafted_from: tool:run-a-script's own row in tools/run-on-a-persons-computer/tool-rows.json (its words, input schema and Node pin), tools/run-on-a-persons-computer/run-a-script.mjs and its test, and the script sandbox's tests (script-sandbox.mjs, test/script-sandbox-child.test.mjs); read them before relying on this kit
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run this script over my tools: find my open rows and return their ids", and give it the body as code, with input for anything the body reads. It runs tool:run-a-script on this Mac, and the answer is the value the body returns.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes code and input in its request and keeps nothing in your records; any row the script reads or writes is a tool call the script makes itself.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI what the script should do, and give it code: a function body that calls call(toolId, input) for each Workshop tool it needs, and returns the value to answer with. Give input for anything the body reads as `input`.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:run-a-script and its input {code, input}, with a request_key that is unique to this run.
3. Read what comes back: {"result": the script's returned value} when it ran, or {"error": what to change}.
4. The script reads files only through the host (no file grant), reaches the network through no route, and cannot start a program; each call it makes runs as you, with the rights the one tool has.

worked_examples.title: Find my open rows and return their ids, through a script
worked_examples.ask: Run this script over my tools: find my open rows and return their ids

input.code: const rows = await call('tool:list-rows', { open: true }); return rows.items.map(row => row.id);

worked_examples.given: A body that makes one call to tool:list-rows and returns the ids of the open rows.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result": ["row-1", "row-2"]} when the Mac runs the tool; an error naming what to change otherwise.
